long_biography.plain_text:
When White Motor's Australian operation failed, Terry Peabody bought the business that had supplied trucks to his earlier industrial companies. He rebuilt it as Western Star's regional distributor, later acquired the Canadian manufacturer and expanded it before selling the group to DaimlerChrysler. The sequence reflected his willingness to turn a supplier problem into an operating platform.

Peabody applied that acquisition instinct to Transpacific Industries, formed around liquid-waste businesses he retained when Pozzolanic was sold. He assembled an Australasian environmental-services group through rapid purchases and added solid-waste operations in Australia and New Zealand. Debt used for expansion left the company exposed during the global financial crisis, prompting a recapitalisation that diluted his stake. He retired as chairman and director in 2010 after more than two decades at the company.
